correctness.rationale: For every reduced p/q and 0<v<q the distance is at least 1/q; when 0 belongs to the residue set, Dirichlet yields <=ell/q; for all nonzero residues, a modular inverse u or q-u gives exactly 1/q. Otherwise choose missing t, a=-t^{-1} mod ell and infinitely many q with aq=-1 mod ell. The integer p=(aq+1)/ell has gcd(p,q)=1. The allowed av residues are 1,...,ell-2, while 0<v/(ell q)<1/ell, forcing the fractional part of vp/q to remain between 1/ell and 1-1/ell. Thus every positive exponent fails. Empty and ell=2 boundary cases and subset counts were checked.

originality.rationale: The source papers introduce the density and prove extremal individual-set examples, whereas the new necessary-and-sufficient statement applies simultaneously to every subset of residues modulo every prime. A prior individual-progressions claim determines the values of each single class and supplies a non-subadditivity example, but cannot imply densities of their arbitrary unions. A constructive rational obstruction using a specifically missing nonzero class supplies the non-implied direction. Directed published-record queries found no close implication match; elementary arguments leave a residual unindexed-priority risk.

value.rationale: This is a complete structural classification of a natural, infinite family of periodic sets for a recently introduced Diophantine invariant, with a sharp missing-unit threshold. It proves the unusual contrast that integer sets occupying (ell-2)/ell of the natural numbers can have zero Diophantine density for arbitrarily large primes; adding either of two specific residue classes restores density one. The result resolves every one of the 2^ell periodic configurations at prime period and is not merely a sample value or a restatement of prior component-wise theorems.
